newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 22.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Wednesday's The Wall Street Journal:

* Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan tells the Senate Budget Committee the economy shows few signs of "inflationary tension" but also hints that he is starting to think of a rate hike on signs that wages are rising.
* International Business Machines Corp quarterly net rose 18 percent, but its revenue growth failed to meet expectations and its gross profit margin fell.
* Boeing Co's decision not to build two superjumbo 747 jets refocuses its rivalry with Airbus Industrie to higher-performance versions of current planes.
* Chase Manhattan Corp Senior Vice Chairman Edward Miller has quit, raising questions of who will be the bank's next chairman.
* Chase Manhattan and Citicorp report healthy fourth quarter results, but Wells Fargo falls short of expectations.
* Allied Irish Banks Plc offers to acquire Dauphin Deposit Corp for $1.36 billion in cash and stock.
* Chrysler Corp's fourth quarter net fell 22 percent, but operating income beat expectations.
* Bell Atlantic Corp, NYNEX Corp, Pacific Telesis Group and SBC Communications Inc either met or slightly exceeded expectations for the quarter.
* Fidelty Investments begins a roadshow to reassure investors that it is back on track.
* Exxon Corp and Royal Dutch/Shell Group's Shell Oil post sharply higher fourth quarter earnings.
* Short interest fell 2.6 percent on the New York Stock Exchange for the month ending January 15.
* A recent survey says American companies reduced the number of coupons issued to the lowest level since 1989.
* Billionaire John Kluge paid $24 million last month for a million shares of Occidental Petroleum.
* A federal appeals court has ruled that limits on mental-health benefits could violate the Americans with Disabilities Act.
* Northwest Airlines Corp's fourth quarter net fell 51 percent, but Continental Airlines Inc's earnings rise 15 percent.

* Benard Schwartz, the 71-year old chairman of Loral Space & Communications Ltd, brushes off the notion that Loral is a "cult" stock, mostly held by his fans. But Loral holders admit that a large part of the stock's price is a tribute to Schwartz's starry-eyed visions of emerging satellite business, which they don't really know how to value. -- Heard on the Street.

* Bond Prices rose yesterday after financial markets concluded that Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's comments suggest that the economy is growing at a pace moderate enough to pose little risk of an inflation flare-up. -- Credit Markets.
